# windows_ntp (Resource)

Manages the Windows Time service (W32Time) time source of a remote Windows machine over SSH/PowerShell.

The time source is a **singleton**: the host always has exactly one, so creating this resource never provisions anything new — it only writes the W32Time registry values in place (`HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time`), runs `w32tm /config /update` (and, by default, a warning-only `w32tm /resync /rediscover`), and deleting it makes no remote change unless `restore_on_destroy` is set. No `w32tm` query output is ever parsed (its text is localised): the registry is the source of truth.

`type` selects the sync type (`NTP`, `NT5DS`, `AllSync`, `NoSync`). `servers` carries the NTP peers (`NtpServer`, `addr,flags` space-separated, order preserved) — required for `NTP`/`AllSync`, forbidden for `NT5DS`/`NoSync`. Peer flags default to `0x9` (SpecialInterval + Client) and are normalised to lower-case.

By default the `W32Time` service is set to `Automatic` start and started (`manage_service`); set it to `false` when a `windows_service` resource owns W32Time. The Terraform resource ID is anchored on `id` (HKLM `MachineGuid`), not on the time source, so it survives configuration changes.

**Destroy is a no-op by default:** a Windows machine cannot exist without a time source; `terraform destroy` only removes the resource from state unless `restore_on_destroy` re-applies the pre-existing values.

Import format: any non-empty ID (its value is ignored; the live time source is adopted, e.g. `current`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Minimal example: point the target host's W32Time service at public NTP
# peers. The time source is a singleton — this resource tunes it in place
# and never provisions anything new. Destroy is a no-op unless
# restore_on_destroy re-applies the pre-existing values captured at
# creation time.
resource "windows_ntp" "this" {
  type = "NTP"

  servers = [
    { address = "0.fr.pool.ntp.org" },
    { address = "1.fr.pool.ntp.org", flags = "0x1" },
  ]

  special_poll_interval_seconds = 900
  reliable                      = false
  ntp_server_enabled            = false
  restore_on_destroy            = true

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly: without this block each
  # operation defaults to 5 minutes, and a stalled registry write,
  # w32tm call or read-back surfaces a timeout diagnostic instead of
  # blocking Terraform indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "5m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "5m"
    delete = "5m"
  }
}

output "type" {
  value       = windows_ntp.this.type
  description = "W32Time sync type."
}

output "current_source" {
  value       = windows_ntp.this.current_source
  description = "Current time source as reported by w32tm /query /source."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `type` (String) W32Time sync type (`W32Time\Parameters\Type`). One of `NTP`, `NT5DS`, `AllSync`, `NoSync`.

### Optional

- `manage_service` (Boolean) When `true`, set the `W32Time` service `StartupType` to `Automatic` and start it before applying. Set to `false` when a `windows_service` resource owns `W32Time`: the service is then left untouched. Default: `true`.
- `max_neg_phase_correction_seconds` (Number) Largest backward clock correction the service may apply, in seconds (`W32Time\Config\MaxNegPhaseCorrection`).
- `max_pos_phase_correction_seconds` (Number) Largest forward clock correction the service may apply, in seconds (`W32Time\Config\MaxPosPhaseCorrection`).
- `ntp_server_enabled` (Boolean) Whether this host answers NTP requests (`W32Time\TimeProviders\NtpServer\Enabled`). Enabling it warns: UDP/123 must be reachable (see `windows_firewall_rule`).
- `reliable` (Boolean) Whether this host is a reliable time source (`W32Time\Config\AnnounceFlags`: `true` writes `5`, `false` writes `10`).
- `restore_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, destroy re-applies the pre-existing W32Time values captured at creation (or import) time. Defaults to `false`: destroy makes no remote change.
- `resync_on_apply` (Boolean) When `true`, run `w32tm /resync /rediscover` after applying. A resync failure surfaces as a warning, never as an error (the peer may be unreachable at apply time). Default: `true`.
- `servers` (Attributes List) NTP peers (`W32Time\Parameters\NtpServer`), in order. Required for type `NTP`/`AllSync`, forbidden for `NT5DS`/`NoSync`. When omitted the host peer list is left untouched. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--servers))
- `special_poll_interval_seconds` (Number) Poll interval in seconds (`W32Time\TimeProviders\NtpClient\SpecialPollInterval`). `16`-`86400`. Only used by peers with the `0x1` (`SpecialInterval`) flag; otherwise a plan-time warning is emitted.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `current_source` (String) Current time source as reported by `w32tm /query /source` (opaque peer name, never parsed). Empty when the query fails (e.g. the service is stopped). Informational only: never produces drift.
- `domain_joined` (Boolean) Whether the host is joined to an Active Directory domain (`Win32_ComputerSystem.PartOfDomain`). Domain-joined hosts should use type `NT5DS` unless this host is the PDC emulator.
- `id` (String) Terraform resource ID. Equal to the host `MachineGuid` (`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid`). Stable across time-source changes.
- `policy_override` (Boolean) Whether Group Policy carries `Type` or `NtpServer` for W32Time (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\W32Time\Parameters`). When `true`, the GPO value wins at the next policy refresh and Terraform-managed values may diverge.

<a id="nestedatt--servers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `servers`

Required:

- `address` (String) Peer hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 address. Must not contain whitespace or commas.

Optional:

- `flags` (String) Per-peer flags. Hex `0x1`-`0xF`, normalised to lower-case. Default: `0x9` (SpecialInterval + Client).


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import the live W32Time time source of the target Windows host.
# The time source is a singleton, so any non-empty import ID is accepted and
# ignored: the live configuration is adopted and becomes the snapshot for a
# later restore_on_destroy.
terraform import windows_ntp.this current
```
